<!-- ============ 1–3. ABOUT: name, description, photo, bio, interests, education, currently ============ -->
<section class="home-wrap about" aria-labelledby="h-name">

  <div class="about-text">
    <!-- class quarto-title-block: tells Quarto this page already has its title header, so it leaves the h1 in place -->
    <header class="about-head quarto-title-block">
      <h1 id="h-name"><span class="first">Honglin</span> Li <span class="name-zh" lang="zh-Hans">(李洪林)</span></h1>
      <p class="about-desc"><span class="segs"><span class="seg">Postdoctoral Fellow</span> <span class="seg">Electrical and Computer Engineering</span> <span class="seg"><a href="https://www.k-state.edu/">Kansas State University</a></span></span></p>
    </header>

    <div class="about-bio">
      <p>I am an energy systems researcher and a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
        at Kansas State University. I build optimization and techno-economic models that show which low-carbon technology
        mixes deliver reliable, affordable energy, and who pays for them. My doctoral research asked when flexibility, from
        hydrogen or from demand, adds value to a low-carbon energy system, at the scale of a plant, a state and the U.S. nuclear
        fleet. My current research asks how large new electricity loads such as AI data centers can be supplied with firm,
        low-carbon power, including small modular reactors.</p>
      <p>My methods include linear, mixed-integer, nonlinear, stochastic and multi-objective optimization, combined with life
        cycle cost and carbon footprint analysis, simulation and reliability modeling. Applications span wind, solar and
        hydrogen systems, regional hydrogen networks, nuclear–hydrogen integration, small modular reactors for data centers,
        grid integration of data centers, and energy storage. My first-author papers appear in <em>Nature Communications</em>,
        <em>Cell Reports Sustainability</em> and the <em>International Journal of Hydrogen Energy</em>, with one accepted in <em>Energy Conversion and Management</em>.</p>
    </div>

<!-- ============ 3a. WHAT I BRING: ability cards, each linking to its evidence elsewhere on the site (website v2,
     reports/07_website_v2_design.md §5). Claims stay general here; the linked sections carry the detail. ============ -->
<section class="home-wrap home-sec" aria-labelledby="h-abilities">
  <div class="section-title"><h2 id="h-abilities">What I bring</h2></div>
  <p class="sec-lede">Each card links to the work that shows it.</p>
  <ul class="ability-grid">
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-lightbulb"></i></span>
      <h3>Independent thinking</h3>
      <p>I look for the interaction that a simpler analysis misses, and explain the mechanism behind results that run against intuition.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="projects/wind-hydrogen.html#insight">Wind–hydrogen</a><a href="projects/npph2.html#insight">Nuclear–hydrogen</a><a href="projects/nuclear-dc.html#insight">SMR cogeneration</a></p>
    </li>
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-layers"></i></span>
      <h3>Research across scales</h3>
      <p>One research question followed from a single wind farm to a state grid and the U.S. nuclear fleet, and its answer led to data-center campuses; each step changed who decides and which uncertainty matters.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="research.html#path">Research path</a><a href="publications.html">Publications</a></p>
    </li>
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-tools"></i></span>
      <h3>Solving applied problems</h3>
      <p>I turn design and investment questions into models built on public market data, hourly operation, policy and cost details, and I state where the answer holds.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="projects.html">Project case studies</a><a href="projects/txh2.html#approach">Texas hydrogen</a><a href="projects/fm-global-internship.html">Industry internship</a></p>
    </li>
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-github"></i></span>
      <h3>Building usable tools</h3>
      <p>Open model frameworks with documented formulations, examples, tests and open-source solvers, so that others can check and reuse the methods.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="software-data.html">Software</a><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021">GitHub</a></p>
    </li>
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-easel"></i></span>
      <h3>Teaching and mentoring</h3>
      <p>Instructor of ECE 685 Power Systems Design; mentored student researchers; I teach students to state a model's assumptions before solving it.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="teaching.html">Teaching</a><a href="learn/index.html">Open course</a><a href="teaching.html#explainers">Interactive explainers</a></p>
    </li>
    <li class="ability">
      <span class="ab-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="bi bi-people"></i></span>
      <h3>Proposals and teamwork</h3>
      <p>Co-PI on an interdisciplinary seed proposal on secure power for Kansas data centers; helped prepare a funded NSF supplement for national-laboratory research.</p>
      <p class="ab-links"><a href="research.html#sei">Proposal</a><a href="cv.html#grant-writing-experience">Grants on the CV</a></p>
    </li>
  </ul>
</section>
